headline: HiddenLayer raises $100M to secure enterprise AI deployments
summary: AI security startup HiddenLayer secures $100 million in Series B funding to protect AI models, agents, and workflows from evolving threats.
details: AI security startup HiddenLayer has successfully raised $100 million in a Series B funding round, led by Delta-v Capital. This funding comes as the market for AI security tools explodes, with Gartner predicting companies will spend $2.83 billion this year on such products.

The company's annual recurring revenue has grown more than 10x in the past year, reaching tens of millions of dollars, driven by new customers in financial services, large tech companies, and government sectors.

HiddenLayer's tools protect AI models, agents, and workflows from adversarial attacks, vulnerabilities, and malicious code injections. They have expanded their offerings to address prompt injection, agent manipulation, and malicious tool use.
The new funding will be used to scale sales and distribution, while continuing to expand engineering and research efforts, with plans for international expansion into Europe and EMEA.

CEO Chris Sestito highlighted the growing threat landscape, particularly the risk of exploiting open-source AI models. HiddenLayer's technology scans various AI file frameworks to ensure the integrity of these models.
The company's runtime security solutions are crucial as AI deployments become more common across businesses, likened to traditional endpoint detection and response (EDR) but tailored for AI.

AI security startup HiddenLayer just closed a $100 million Series B funding round, highlighting the booming market for AI protection tools.

AI security startup HiddenLayer has successfully raised $100 million in a Series B funding round, led by Delta-v Capital. This funding comes as the market for AI security tools explodes, with Gartner predicting companies will spend $2.83 billion this year on such products.

The company's annual recurring revenue has grown more than 10x in the past year, reaching tens of millions of dollars, driven by new customers in financial services, large tech companies, and government sectors.

HiddenLayer's tools protect AI models, agents, and workflows from adversarial attacks, vulnerabilities, and malicious code injections. They have expanded their offerings to address prompt injection, agent manipulation, and malicious tool use.

The new funding will be used to scale sales and distribution, while continuing to expand engineering and research efforts, with plans for international expansion into Europe and EMEA.

CEO Chris Sestito highlighted the growing threat landscape, particularly the risk of exploiting open-source AI models. HiddenLayer's technology scans various AI file frameworks to ensure the integrity of these models.

The company's runtime security solutions are crucial as AI deployments become more common across businesses, likened to traditional endpoint detection and response (EDR) but tailored for AI.
